--- title: "Macro × debt: overnight Selic instead of the target rate and check of the correlation data" description: "Do the correlations with the Selic rate change when the effective (overnight) rate is used instead of the target? Are the macro data in the correlations right in source, unit, frequency, lag and coverage? Where does the correlation between employment and stock come from?" date: 2026-10-23 jupyter: python3 --- **Data:** `macro.duckdb` (table `MACRO`, SGS/BCB series), the SGS 4189 series downloaded from the BCB on 23/10/2026 and the aggregates of the full EDA (monthly series of collections, payers and new CDAs; annual stock of the VAT (ICMS) panel). `extracao=2026-03`. **Window:** 2016 to 2025. 2026 is left out (decision of 23/10/2026): the year was incomplete in the debt data (up to March) and in the macro series. **Status:** exploration and data check. Correlation is not effect. ## 1. Overnight Selic instead of the target Selic (MAC-03) **Sources checked in the BCB open data catalogue on 23/10/2026:** - **SGS 432**, used until now: *Interest rate, Selic target set by Copom*, in % p.a. It is the target, which changes only at Copom meetings. - **SGS 4189**: *Interest rate, Selic compounded over the month, annualised on a 252-day basis*, in % p.a., monthly. According to the BCB, it is the "adjusted average rate of one-business-day repurchase operations backed by federal government securities held in custody at Selic", that is, the effective (overnight) Selic, already in the same unit as the target. - **Discarded:** SGS 1178 (Selic annualised on a 252-day basis) is the same rate at daily frequency. The monthly version 4189 avoids an extra aggregation. ::: {#tbl-selic .cell tbl-cap='Target Selic (monthly mean of the daily series 432) and overnight Selic (4189), 2016 to 2025.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Removing 2026 and removing 2020 lowers the value slightly, but the correlation in levels stays high. - **Differences:** in first differences, Pearson stays high, but Spearman is close to zero and negative. The gap between the two shows that the correlation of the changes depends on a few points. Without the changes involving 2020, the correlation changes sign and the interval includes zero. All of the correlation of the changes comes from 2020: employment fell and the summed stock of the panel also fell, and both rose again afterwards. - **Trend and 2020:** removing only the linear trend does not eliminate the correlation, and without 2020 the interval includes zero. The pattern "rises, falls in 2020, rises again" is the same in both series. - **The 2020 fall seems to come from the extraction:** the stock falls from BRL 410.6 bn (2019) to BRL 328.9 bn (2020), and the number of CDAs in the panel falls with it (from 2.18 mn to 1.81 mn). Such a large and simultaneous fall in the CDA count suggests that it comes from how the 2020 data were extracted (CDAs that leave and return to the panel, or extraction coverage), not from the economy. This should be checked when the corrected DEBITO table arrives. **What not to conclude:** with 9 or 10 points, none of these correlations supports a claim in the article. ## 3. They are in BRL of Dec 2025. | | PNAD Contínua (2.2) | Confirmed in the IBGE and SGS metadata: the monthly value of unemployment (24369) and employed persons (24379) is the **moving quarter** ending in the month, and neighbouring months share two months of interviews. In the annual series, the mean of the four calendar quarters (Mar, Jun, Sep, Dec) is used. In the monthly series, the value stays as it is, with this caveat: the monthly change is that of a moving quarter, not of a month. | | Selic | Overnight (4189) instead of the target (MAC-03). | | 2020 fall in the stock (2.5) | **Cannot be corrected now:** depends on the corrected DEBITO table (EQ-02/EQ-05). See the warning below. | ::: {.callout-warning title="Warning: employment × stock and the year 2020"} The annual correlation between stock and employed persons rests on the common trend and on the 2020 fall. In that year the panel's stock falls from BRL 410.6 bn to BRL 328.9 bn and the CDA count falls with it, which looks like an effect of the DEBITO extraction, not of the economy. ``` ::: ::: **How to read:** "before" is the number saved by the full EDA, "after" is the same pair with the corrections. In the monthly series, the largest change is that of deflated corporate credit (see the summary by series). In the other series, the change comes from the 2025 cut-off and, in the rows with k ≥ 1, from the switch of lag convention. In the annual series, with 10 points, the confidence intervals are wide (CI columns), and several correlations change considerably with the switch to real values and calendar quarters. **What not to conclude:** the corrections remove construction biases, but do not solve the sample size (10 years), the autocorrelation of the monthly series or the 2020 fall in the stock. The employment × stock correlation stays out of the text until the corrected DEBITO. ## Summary of the check - **Source and unit:** the 11 series come from the SGS/BCB, with name and unit recorded in the table. Target (432) and overnight (4189) are in the same unit (% p.a.). - **Coverage:** the correlations saved in the full EDA include 2026, which is incomplete. This subsection redoes the computations for 2016 to 2025. - **Nominal × real:** monthly GDP and corporate credit enter in current BRL, with no deflator or log. In levels, the correlation with the nominal stock captures the common trend. - **Frequency:** daily series (target, PTAX) become monthly means. The monthly PNAD Contínua is a moving quarter (checked on 26/10/2026); subsection 3 uses calendar quarters in the annual series. - **Lags:** there are two conventions in the EDA (lagged macro and lagged Y). Subsection 3 uses only the lagged macro. - **Employment × stock:** the correlation replicates (0.873) and rests on the common trend and the 2020 trough, which also appears in the CDA count. Before interpreting, check the 2020 stock in the corrected DEBITO. See 2.5. ::: {#cell-cache .cell execution_count=18} ::: {#cache .cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=18} ```{=html}
